subject: Post-demo qualification: side-by-side latency & throughput probe with Vertex Labs
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Park <oliver@vertexlabs.ai>; Vertex Labs Technical Ops <ops@vertexlabs.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 May 2029 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: proposed latency/throughput probe (p95/p99 + tokens/sec)

Hi Oliver — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can qualify the production delta you asked about vs the hyperscaler API: 

Summary of ask from your team:
- Side-by-side probe of your current inference endpoint vs Redwood hosted endpoint for the same model family and prompt mix.
- Measure p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, and throughput at 1, 5, 20 qps profiles.
- Run in us-west-2 and us-east-1, with both short (<=64 tokens) and long (>=1024 tokens) sequences.

What we propose (attached plan + config):
- Mutual test harness: run 30-minute A/B windows at 1/5/20 QPS, capture token-level timing, p95/p99, and tail behaviors (microbursts).
- Use same request payloads and sampling of user prompts you provided in demo.
- Redwood will bring a probe harness (redwood_probe_harness.sh) and a baseline YAML for workload config (vertex_lab_latency_probe.yaml).

Requests from your side:
- Provide service account/API key for a read-only test client (ops@vertexlabs.ai can create), plus a sample of ~500 production-like prompts (anonymized) if available.
- Confirm whether cold-starts are expected (container spin-up) and whether there are any rate-limiting headers we should honor.

Tentative schedule: can you confirm a 2-hour window next Wed 2029-05-15 between 09:00–12:00 PT? We can run the 3 probes in sequence and do a quick sync at the end.

Attachments: proposed config + short post-demo notes.

Thanks —
Neha
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0124

---
Attachments: vertex_lab_latency_probe.yaml (text), redwood_probe_harness.sh (script), post_demo_notes.pdf (summary)

Date: Thu, 9 May 2029 17:03:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: proposed latency/throughput probe (p95/p99 + tokens/sec)

Neha — appreciate the clear plan. A few clarifications from our side before we lock the window: 

1) We have two endpoint tiers: standard and low-latency edge. For fairness we want to compare Redwood against our low-latency tier. Can you confirm Redwood will spin up instances in us-west-2 edge subnet?
2) Sample prompts: we can share a sanitized set (about 420 prompts). Ops will drop into the Drive link you suggested.
3) API keys: ops@vertexlabs.ai will send a test key limited to 100 qps and scoped to the probe IPs you provide.

Wed 2029-05-15 09:00–12:00 PT works for us. Can you include Jordan and Marissa on the run so we can coordinate metrics collection?

Oliver

Thanks — I can take the lead on the Redwood side for the harness. Proposed internal plan: 
- Day-before prep: validate payloads in staging, ensure identical model weights & tokenization between endpoints. Marissa, can you confirm we have a quantized variant matched to the Vertex config?
- Run plan: 3x 30-minute windows (1 QPS, 5 QPS, 20 QPS). Capture per-token timing hooks, p50/p95/p99, CPU/GPU utilization, and network egress.
- Data sync: we’ll push raw logs to the shared Drive folder and produce a one-page runbook with key charts.

Marissa — looping you for the quantization/variant confirmation and to schedule a short dry run Tue 2029-05-14 10:00 PT. Rishi, can you add a canary to ensure no cross-tenant cache leakage?

Jordan
Engineering Lead, Inference Performance | Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 13 May 2029 08:22:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: proposed latency/throughput probe (p95/p99 + tokens/sec)

Confirmed — we have a quantized int8 variant that matches the Vertex model family (same architecture, same checkpoint). Notes: 
- For long-sequence runs (>=1024 tokens) we'll disable KV-compression so results reflect real-world tail behavior.
- Will include both a fully-quantized path and a float32 baseline so we can compare accuracy regressions vs throughput.

I scheduled the dry run Tue 2029-05-14 10:00 PT and added the test configs to the Drive link. Attaching the quick guide and the YAML for the run.

Marissa
